trajectory.patch:
The compilation errors indicate a problem with preprocessor macro expansion, specifically with token pasting (`##`). The errors like `pasting ")" and "_P_" does not give a valid preprocessing token` occur when a macro argument that is not a single token (e.g., it's enclosed in parentheses) is used with a token-pasting operator.

The root cause is in `include/zephyr/devicetree.h`, where the `DT_CAT` family of macros is defined to perform token pasting without first expanding their arguments. This contradicts the comments in the file, which state that expansion should happen before pasting. When a macro that expands to a node identifier is passed to another devicetree macro (like `DT_PROP` or `DT_FOREACH_CHILD`), the token pasting fails.

The fix is to modify the `DT_CAT` macros to use a two-step macro expansion, which is a standard C preprocessor technique to ensure arguments are expanded before they are concatenated. This will resolve the token pasting errors and the subsequent chain of compilation failures.

<include/zephyr/devicetree.h>
<<<<<<<< SEARCH
#define DT_CAT(a1, a2) a1 ## a2
/** @brief Concatenation helper, 3 arguments */
#define DT_CAT3(a1, a2, a3) a1 ## a2 ## a3
/** @brief Concatenation helper, 4 arguments */
#define DT_CAT4(a1, a2, a3, a4) a1 ## a2 ## a3 ## a4
/** @brief Internal concatenation helper, 5 arguments */
#define DT_CAT5(a1, a2, a3, a4, a5) a1 ## a2 ## a3 ## a4 ## a5
/** @brief Concatenation helper, 6 arguments */
#define DT_CAT6(a1, a2, a3, a4, a5, a6) a1 ## a2 ## a3 ## a4 ## a5 ## a6
/** @brief concatenation helper, 7 arguments */
#define DT_CAT7(a1, a2, a3, a4, a5, a6, a7) \
	a1 ## a2 ## a3 ## a4 ## a5 ## a6 ## a7
/** @brief concatenation helper, 8 arguments */
#define DT_CAT8(a1, a2, a3, a4, a5, a6, a7, a8) \
	a1 ## a2 ## a3 ## a4 ## a5 ## a6 ## a7 ## a8
